subject: general
question: The rivers Arun, Barun and Tamur are part of the________ river system.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kosi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Kosi is a 720 km long trans-boundary river which flows through Nepal, Tibet and India. 
 
• It drains the northern slopes in Tibet and southern slopes in Nepal. It is also known as Saptakoshi due to its seven upper tributaries, namely, the Indrawati, the Sun Koshi, the Tama Koshi, the Likhu, the Dudh Koshi, the Arun and the Tamor. 
 
• The Saptakoshi after flowing through the Himalayas crosses into Bihar where it branches into distributaries before joining the Ganges near Kursela in Katihar district.
 
• Kamala, Bagmati and Budhi Gandak are the major tributaries of the river in India.
 
• The real name of Koshi is "Kaushiki". It is also known as "Sorrow of Bihar". The river gained this name because of its unstable nature which results in heavy annual flood during the rainy season. Extensive Soil Erosion and Landslides have produced a heap of silt yield which is one of the highest in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sindhu River:

 
 
• Also referred to as the “Sindhu”, the Indus River is a long transboundary river in the Continent of Asia that is shared by the countries of China, India, and Pakistan.
 
• Rising in Western Tibet, the river flows for more than 3,180km and is considered as one of the world’s largest rivers and the longest river in Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Krishna River**
 
 
• The Krishna is the second important river in south India.
 
• It takes birth at Mahabaleshwar and flows 1,392 km eastwards to join the Bay of Bengal.
 
• It flows for only 480 km. through Karnataka.
 
• Left bank tributaries- Bhima, Musi, Dindi, Paleru, Munneru.
 
• Right bank tributaries- Venna, Koyna, Panchganga, Dudhaganga, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Tungabhadra.
 
• The largest tributary of Krishna is the Tungabhadra river.
 
• The Koyna is a small tributary but is known for Koyna Dam.
 
• 
 
The Krishna forms a large delta with a shoreline of about 120 km. 

 
 
• Irrigation and hydroelectric power generation from the Krishna river system have benefited Northern Karnataka.
 
• Hydroelectric power stations from Krishna are:
 
 
• Almatti Hydroelectric Project- Vijayapura
 
• Bhadra Hydroelectric Project- Chickmagaluru
 
• Ghataprabha Hydroelectric Project- Belagavi
 
 
 
 
 
• **Godavari river**
 
 
• The Godavari is the biggest east-flowing river in India.
 
• The Godavari basin falls in the Deccan plateau.
 
• The Godavari river rises from Trimbakeshwar, Nashik Maharashtra.
 
• The Godavari river is outfalls in the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The total length of the Godavari is 1465 km.
 
• The Godavari is the main river of Telangana state.
 
• About 69% of the Godavari catchment area lies in Telangana.
 
• Apart from Telangana, Godavari is spread in the states of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Chattisgarh, and Orissa.
